newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: U.S. firm wins Guatemala railroad concession.
newsitem.headline: U.S. firm wins Guatemala railroad concession.

text.p: Railroad Development Corp. of Pittsburgh on Friday won the right to run Guatemala's deteriorating railroad, a major advance in the country's privatization program.

"This is a clear demonstration of the Guatemalan government's interest to put into working order public services," Gustavo Seravia, a member of a presidential commission working to streamline and strengthen public services, said.

The company won the exclusive concession for 504 miles (813 km) of right of way during 50 years, which can be extended to 100 years. It will pay 5 percent of gross income in the first two years and 10 percent in the remaining 48 years, said Andes Porras of the Guatemalan Railroad Company (FEGUA).
Plans are to renovate the railroad, which stopped operating year ago, beginning with the Atlantic-Pacific route from Guatemala City to Puerto Barrios on the East coast, he said.
Congress must approve the contract, a process that could take six months.

The railroad system becomes the first public institution to fall under a government privatization program that targets 16 government-run services this year and could include some 56 in all. Other privatization projects include sale of two government-owned electric plants and the telephone system.

The railroad includes a route to Tecun Uman at the Mexican border, and a connecting line to the frontier with El Salvador. Two other connecting lines run from ports on the West coast to Pacific slope cities of Escuintla and Retalhuleu.
